pictures.scene: Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue on Yom Kippur — the whole congregation crowded in under the stone arches of the synagogue on the holy day, the men below wrapped in white and black striped prayer shawls, one bent over the open book on the reading desk with his hand to his ear, another with his hand pressed hard to his forehead, a bearded man in a tall fur hat carrying the mantled scroll in both arms with its star and its Hebrew lettering, a boy in a flowered coat standing at the front looking out at us, and the women leaning over the gallery rail above in silver head-cloths and fur-trimmed red and green, now the feast of unleavened bread, called the passover, was approaching, …
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Judas Returning the Thirty Pieces of Silver — inside the dark temple hall a man has thrown himself on his knees on the stone floor, wringing his hands together and bowing his head almost to the ground before the priests, his hair torn out at the front and his coat hanging off one shoulder, the high priest in a purple robe and a gold sash turning away from him with one hand pushed out, an old man with a white beard and others in fur hats crowding in behind to stare at him, a great gold lamp hanging down out of the shadows above, and the silver coins lying scattered in a little heap on the boards at the front of the picture, and judas went to discuss with the chief priests and temple officers how he might betray jesus to them, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_judas_returning_the_thirty_pieces_of_silver

pictures.scene: Reymerswaele, The Tax Collectors — two men lean in close over the ledger in a cramped back office hung about with papers, the one in the great red fur hat and the blue gown bent right down over the open book with spectacles pinched on his nose and a pen in his ringed hand, writing the sum in, the other behind him in a green cap grinning sideways out of the picture with his face all creased up, one finger pointing down at the page and the other hand closed over the coins, the brown coins and a little pair of scales lying about on the table, and above them a shelf of rolled papers, a candlestick and a brass dish, they were delighted and agreed to give him money, …
pictures.name: pd_reymerswaele_the_tax_collectors

pictures.scene: Zurbaran, Agnus Dei — a young white ram lying on its side on a plain stone slab in the dark, nothing else in the picture at all, the light falling only on the thick curled fleece and on the long pale face laid flat along the stone, the eye half shut, the nose soft and pink, one heavy horn curving back around the ear and the other over the crown of the head, and all the rest of the picture black behind it, then came the day of unleavened bread on which the passover lamb was to be sacrificed, …
pictures.name: pd_zurbaran_agnus_dei

pictures.scene: Velazquez, The Waterseller of Seville — an old water carrier in a torn brown cloak stands in the dark with one hand round the great pale water jar in front of him, the clay of it ribbed and beaded with wet, his other hand holding out a glass of water across the top of it, a boy in a white collar taking the glass with both hands and looking up at him, a third man drinking behind them with his face half lost in the shadow, and a second jar standing on a stool at the left, he answered, when you enter the city, a man carrying a jug of water will meet you, follow him to the house he enters, …
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_waterseller_seville

pictures.scene: Ancher, Sunlight in the Blue Room — an upstairs room in strong afternoon sun, the whole left wall painted deep blue with the shape of the window thrown across it in white and pale blue light, the tall window at the back hung with gold curtains and standing open onto the day, a mirror and a corner cupboard beside it, a bare wooden floor with the sunlight lying along the boards in yellow stripes, chairs standing about a little work table, and in the middle of it all a fair-haired girl in a blue dress sitting with her head bent over the sewing in her hands, and he will show you a large upper room, already furnished, make preparations there, …
pictures.name: pd_ancher_sunlight_in_the_blue_room

pictures.scene: Bouts, Christ in the House of Simon — the Lord sits at the end of a trestle table in a stone room with one hand raised in blessing and His head bowed, a long dark robe, His bare feet showing under the table, the white cloth spread with round loaves, a green glass and a fish on a pewter dish, the bearded host in a blue jewelled cap and a yellow gown leaning in at His side, an open colonnade at the left looking out over a river and fields, and on the floor at the front a woman in red and green and blue bowed right down with her face almost on the tiles, drying His feet with her long loose hair, her little jar standing beside her, when the hour had come, jesus reclined at the table with his apostles, …
pictures.name: pd_bouts_christ_in_the_house_of_simon

lines.text: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, was approaching,
and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death; for they feared the people.
Then Satan entered Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.
And Judas went to discuss with the chief priests and temple officers how he might betray Jesus to them.
They were delighted and agreed to give him money.
Judas consented, and began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus to them in the absence of a crowd.
Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare for us to eat the Passover.
Where do You want us to prepare it? they asked.
He answered, When you enter the city, a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him to the house he enters,
and say to the owner of that house, The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?
And he will show you a large upper room, already furnished. Make preparations there.
So they went and found it just as Jesus had told them. And they prepared the Passover.
When the hour had come, Jesus reclined at the table with His apostles.
And He said to them, I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering.
For I tell you that I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
After taking the cup, He gave thanks and said, Take this and divide it among yourselves.
For I tell you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on until the kingdom of God comes.
And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.
In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
Look! The hand of My betrayer is with Mine on the table.
Indeed, the Son of Man will go as it has been determined, but woe to that man who betrays Him.
Then they began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this.
A dispute also arose among the disciples as to which of them would be considered the greatest.
So Jesus declared, The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them call themselves benefactors.
But you shall not be like them. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
For who is greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are the ones who have stood by Me in My trials.
And I bestow on you a kingdom, just as My Father has bestowed one on Me,
so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift each of you like wheat.
But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.
Lord, said Peter, I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.
But Jesus replied, I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.
Then Jesus asked them, When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything? Nothing, they answered.
Now, however, He told them, the one with a purse should take it, and likewise a bag; and the one without a sword should sell his cloak and buy one.
For I tell you that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Me: And He was numbered with the transgressors. For what is written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.
So they said, Look, Lord, here are two swords. That is enough, He answered.
Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed Him.
When He came to the place, He told them, Pray that you will not enter into temptation.
And He withdrew about a stone's throw beyond them, where He knelt down and prayed,
Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours be done.
Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him.
And in His anguish, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.
When Jesus rose from prayer and returned to the disciples, He found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow.
Why are you sleeping? He asked. Get up and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.
While He was still speaking, a crowd arrived, led by the man called Judas, one of the Twelve. He approached Jesus to kiss Him.
But Jesus asked him, Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?
Those around Jesus saw what was about to happen and said, Lord, should we strike with our swords?
And one of them struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear.
But Jesus answered, No more of this! And He touched the man's ear and healed him.
Then Jesus said to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him, Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?
Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me. But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.
Then they seized Jesus, led Him away, and took Him into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed at a distance.
When those present had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.
A servant girl saw him seated in the firelight and looked intently at him. This man also was with Him, she said.
But Peter denied it. Woman, I do not know Him, he said.
A short time later, someone else saw him and said, You also are one of them. But Peter said, Man, I am not.
About an hour later, another man insisted, Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.
Man, I do not know what you are talking about, Peter replied. While he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.
And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word that the Lord had spoken to him: Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times.
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
The men who were holding Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him.
They blindfolded Him and kept demanding, Prophesy! Who hit You?
And they said many other blasphemous things against Him.
At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together. They led Jesus into their Sanhedrin and said,
If You are the Christ, tell us. Jesus answered, If I tell you, you will not believe. And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.
But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.
So they all asked, Are You then the Son of God? He replied, You say that I am.
Why do we need any more testimony? they declared. We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips.
